items.q: Which tissue carries water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the leaves?
items.qAf: Watter weefsel vervoer water en opgeloste minerale vanaf die wortels na die blare?
items.explain: Xylem carries water and minerals upwards from the roots.
items.explainAf: Xileem vervoer water en minerale opwaarts vanaf die wortels.

items.q: Which tissue carries sugar made in the leaves to the rest of the plant?
items.qAf: Watter weefsel vervoer suiker wat in die blare gemaak word na die res van die plant?
items.explain: Phloem moves sugars from where they are made (sources, such as leaves) to where they are needed (sinks, such as roots and fruit).
items.explainAf: Floëem beweeg suikers van waar hulle gemaak word (bronne, soos blare) na waar hulle nodig is (opvangplekke, soos wortels en vrugte).

items.q: A ring of bark is removed from a tree trunk. Which tissue is removed, cutting sugar supply to the roots?
items.qAf: ’n Ring bas word van ’n boomstam verwyder. Watter weefsel word verwyder, wat die suikeraanvoer na die wortels afsny?
items.explain: Phloem lies in the bark, so removing it stops sugar reaching the roots.
items.explainAf: Floëem lê in die bas, dus stop die verwydering suiker om die wortels te bereik.

items.q: Transpiration mainly takes place through the:
items.qAf: Transpirasie vind hoofsaaklik plaas deur die:
items.explain: Most water vapour leaves the plant through the stomata in the leaves.
items.explainAf: Die meeste waterdamp verlaat die plant deur die huidmondjies in die blare.

items.q: What mainly pulls water up through the xylem?
items.qAf: Wat trek water hoofsaaklik op deur die xileem?
items.explain: Water evaporating from the leaves creates a pull that draws a continuous column of water upwards.
items.explainAf: Water wat uit die blare verdamp, skep ’n trek wat ’n aaneenlopende kolom water opwaarts trek.

items.q: On a hot, dry, windy day, transpiration increases. Why?
items.qAf: Op ’n warm, droë, winderige dag neem transpirasie toe. Hoekom?
options: The water vapour gradient between leaf and air increases
optionsAf: Die waterdampgradiënt tussen blaar en lug neem toe
Die wortels hou op om water op te neem
items.explain: Dry, moving air takes water vapour away faster, increasing the gradient and the rate of transpiration.
items.explainAf: Droë, bewegende lug neem waterdamp vinniger weg, wat die gradiënt en die transpirasiespoed verhoog.

items.q: The tissue that carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves.
items.qAf: Die weefsel wat water en minerale van die wortels na die blare vervoer.

items.q: The tissue that carries food (sugars) around the plant.
items.qAf: Die weefsel wat voedsel (suikers) deur die plant vervoer.

items.q: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant.
items.qAf: Die verlies van waterdamp uit die blare van ’n plant.

items.q: The cells on either side of a stoma that control its opening.
items.qAf: Die selle aan weerskante van ’n huidmondjie wat sy opening beheer.

items.text: Water enters root hairs by [[]]. The upward pull of water caused by transpiration is called the transpiration [[]].
items.textAf: Water gaan wortelhare binne deur [[]]. Die opwaartse trek van water wat deur transpirasie veroorsaak word, word die transpirasie[[]] genoem.

items.q: Transpiration is faster on a hot, dry, windy day.
items.qAf: Transpirasie is vinniger op ’n warm, droë, winderige dag.
items.explain: True. Heat, low humidity and wind all increase the rate of evaporation from the leaves.
items.explainAf: Waar. Hitte, lae humiditeit en wind verhoog almal die tempo van verdamping uit die blare.

items.q: Xylem vessels are made of living cells with cytoplasm.
items.qAf: Xileemvate bestaan uit lewende selle met sitoplasma.
items.explain: False. Mature xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes strengthened with lignin.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Volwasse xileemvate is dooie, hol buise wat met lignien versterk is.

items.q: Match each factor in column A with its effect on the rate of transpiration in column B.
items.qAf: Pas elke faktor in kolom A by sy uitwerking op die transpirasietempo in kolom B.

items.q: Describe how a potometer can be used to compare the rate of transpiration in still air and in moving air.
items.qAf: Beskryf hoe ’n potometer gebruik kan word om die transpirasietempo in stil lug en in bewegende lug te vergelyk.
points: Measure how far the air bubble moves in a set time with the shoot in still air.
Repeat with a fan blowing on the shoot, keeping everything else the same.
The faster the bubble moves, the faster the rate of transpiration (water uptake).
pointsAf: Meet hoe ver die lugborrel in ’n vaste tyd beweeg met die loot in stil lug.
Herhaal met ’n waaier wat op die loot blaas, en hou alles anders dieselfde.
Hoe vinniger die borrel beweeg, hoe vinniger is die transpirasietempo (wateropname).
